questions.prompt: Which element of art is most directly used to create contour and outline in drawing?
options: Line
Kiln
Loom
Wax
questions.correctAnswer: Line
questions.explanation: Line defines edges, contours and movement in a drawing before other details are added.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify elements of 2D art used in drawing.

questions.prompt: In one-point perspective, what is the point where receding parallel lines appear to meet?
options: Vanishing point
Focal stitch
Resist point
Warp point
questions.correctAnswer: Vanishing point
questions.explanation: A vanishing point creates the illusion that parallel edges move away into depth.
questions.learningOutcome: Name key features of linear perspective in drawing.

questions.prompt: Which drawing subject is arranged from objects placed together for observation?
options: Still life composition
Trademark layout
Batik fabric
Updraught kiln
questions.correctAnswer: Still life composition
questions.explanation: Still life drawing uses arranged objects so learners can observe form, proportion, light and shadow.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise still life as an observational drawing subject.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a portfolio folder in Visual Arts?
options: To store and present artworks safely
To heat clay during firing
To mix dyes for fabric
To carve relief forms
questions.correctAnswer: To store and present artworks safely
questions.explanation: A portfolio folder protects artworks and helps organise them for review or presentation.
questions.learningOutcome: State the purpose of a portfolio folder for artwork presentation.

questions.prompt: Which painting technique applies thin transparent colour over a surface?
options: Wash technique
Pellet technique
Plain weaving
Relief carving
questions.correctAnswer: Wash technique
questions.explanation: A wash uses diluted colour to build light, atmosphere and broad tonal areas.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify painting techniques used to create tonal effects.

questions.prompt: Which wash changes gradually from dark to light across a painting area?
options: Graded wash
Flat wash
Wax resist
Plain weave
questions.correctAnswer: Graded wash
questions.explanation: A graded wash varies tone smoothly, while a flat wash keeps an even tone.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish common wash effects in painting.

questions.prompt: Which technique sprays paint from a brush to create speckled colour effects?
options: Brush-spray painting
Coil weaving
Leather thonging
Wedging
questions.correctAnswer: Brush-spray painting
questions.explanation: Brush-spray painting flicks or sprays colour from a brush to form dotted or misted effects.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify brush-spray painting as a picture-making technique.

questions.prompt: Which art technique builds an image by pasting cut or torn materials onto a surface?
options: Collage
Calligraphy
Vitrification
Firing
questions.correctAnswer: Collage
questions.explanation: Collage combines papers, fabrics or other materials on a support to create a composition.
questions.learningOutcome: Define collage as a 2D picture-making technique.

questions.prompt: Which feature in collage occurs when one shape partly covers another?
options: Overlapping
Porosity
Ascender
Warping
questions.correctAnswer: Overlapping
questions.explanation: Overlapping helps show depth and spatial order in a collage composition.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify visual features used in collage making.

questions.prompt: In calligraphy, which part of a lowercase letter rises above the main body line?
options: Ascender
Descender
Selvedge
Slip
questions.correctAnswer: Ascender
questions.explanation: Ascenders are the upward parts of letters such as b, d and h above the body height.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic aspects of lowercase calligraphy.

questions.prompt: In calligraphy, which part of a lowercase letter extends below the baseline?
options: Descender
Ascender
Void
Weft
questions.correctAnswer: Descender
questions.explanation: Descenders are the lower parts of letters such as g, j, p and y.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the descender in lowercase calligraphy.

questions.prompt: Which design item identifies a product, group or business through a distinctive symbol or lettering?
options: Trademark
Kiln shelf
Clay slip
Warp thread
questions.correctAnswer: Trademark
questions.explanation: A trademark uses a recognisable sign, symbol or lettering to identify a product or organisation.
questions.learningOutcome: Define a trademark in graphic design.

questions.prompt: Which fabric decoration method creates patterns by tying fabric before applying dye?
options: Tie and dye
Batik
Carving
Modelling
questions.correctAnswer: Tie and dye
questions.explanation: Tied areas resist dye penetration, producing patterned effects after the ties are removed.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify tie and dye as a resist fabric decoration method.

questions.prompt: Which batik material is commonly applied to fabric as a dye resist?
options: Wax
Sand
Clay pellets
Sisal fibre
questions.correctAnswer: Wax
questions.explanation: Wax blocks selected fabric areas so dye affects only the unwaxed parts.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify wax as the resist material used in batik.

questions.prompt: Which clay property allows it to be shaped without cracking immediately?
options: Plasticity
Solubility
Transparency
Elastic bounce
questions.correctAnswer: Plasticity
questions.explanation: Plasticity is the ability of moist clay to be formed and retain shape during modelling.
questions.learningOutcome: Name properties of clay used in pottery.

questions.prompt: Which pottery process heats clay objects until they become hard and durable?
options: Firing
Fringing
Mounting
Lettering
questions.correctAnswer: Firing
questions.explanation: Firing changes dry clay into a stronger ceramic object through controlled heat.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify firing as a pottery production process.

questions.prompt: Why is proportion important when drawing a still life group?
options: It keeps the relative sizes of objects believable
It makes all objects the same colour
It replaces the need for observation
It turns the drawing into a sculpture
questions.correctAnswer: It keeps the relative sizes of objects believable
questions.explanation: Proportion compares the size of parts to each other and to the whole arrangement.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of proportion in observational drawing.

questions.prompt: What does shading mainly help an artist show in a drawing?
options: Light, shadow and volume
Kiln temperature only
Fabric dye recipe only
Marketing price only
questions.correctAnswer: Light, shadow and volume
questions.explanation: Shading uses tonal values to make flat drawings suggest three-dimensional form.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how value supports form in drawing.

questions.prompt: Why does an artist use two-point perspective for the corner of a building?
options: Two visible sides recede toward different vanishing points
Only one front face is visible with no depth
The building must be viewed from directly above
All vertical lines must curve into circles
questions.correctAnswer: Two visible sides recede toward different vanishing points
questions.explanation: Two-point perspective is suitable when a corner faces the viewer and each side recedes in a different direction.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain when two-point perspective is appropriate.

questions.prompt: What is the advantage of arranging objects with overlap in still life drawing?
options: It helps create depth and visual relationship between objects
It makes every object invisible
It removes the need for a light source
It prevents the use of line
questions.correctAnswer: It helps create depth and visual relationship between objects
questions.explanation: Overlapping places objects in front of or behind others, strengthening spatial depth.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain compositional choices in still life drawing.

questions.prompt: Why should a portfolio folder be labelled clearly?
options: It helps identify the owner, class and artwork set during assessment
It makes the artwork heavier
It changes drawings into paintings
It replaces feedback from peers
questions.correctAnswer: It helps identify the owner, class and artwork set during assessment
questions.explanation: Clear labelling supports organisation, storage, retrieval and presentation of artwork.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain good portfolio management practice.

questions.prompt: Why is a flat wash useful in painting a clear sky?
options: It gives an even area of colour without strong tonal change
It carves raised texture into clay
It ties fabric tightly before dyeing
It creates only letter descenders
questions.correctAnswer: It gives an even area of colour without strong tonal change
questions.explanation: A flat wash produces a uniform tone, which suits broad even areas such as a calm sky.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain uses of flat wash in painting.

questions.prompt: Why is a graded wash useful when painting distance in a landscape?
options: It can suggest atmospheric depth through gradual tonal change
It makes the paper waterproof forever
It removes all need for composition
It creates a ceramic glaze by itself
questions.correctAnswer: It can suggest atmospheric depth through gradual tonal change
questions.explanation: Gradual changes in tone can make distant areas appear softer or lighter, supporting depth.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how wash technique can create atmospheric depth.

questions.prompt: Why is colour harmony important in a pictorial composition?
options: It helps colours relate pleasantly and support unity
It ensures every colour clashes strongly
It makes brush cleaning unnecessary
It replaces the subject of the artwork
questions.correctAnswer: It helps colours relate pleasantly and support unity
questions.explanation: Colour harmony makes the composition feel visually connected while still allowing variety.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of colour harmony in painting.

questions.prompt: Why can brush-spray painting be effective for a background texture?
options: It creates repeated small marks that can suggest mist, dust or surface grain
It produces only straight measured lines
It joins clay pellets permanently
It calculates the selling price
questions.correctAnswer: It creates repeated small marks that can suggest mist, dust or surface grain
questions.explanation: The speckled marks from brush-spray technique can add texture and atmosphere.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain expressive uses of brush-spray painting.

questions.prompt: Why should a collage composition have a clear focal area?
options: It guides the viewer to the main idea of the artwork
It prevents any material from being pasted
It makes all shapes the same size
It turns paper into cloth
questions.correctAnswer: It guides the viewer to the main idea of the artwork
questions.explanation: A focal area gives the viewer a visual starting point and supports clear communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of dominance in collage composition.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains a multimedia collage?
options: It combines more than one material or technique in one composition
It uses only a single pencil line
It is made only by firing clay
It is a woven fabric with no image
questions.correctAnswer: It combines more than one material or technique in one composition
questions.explanation: Multimedia collage may combine paper, fabric, found objects, paint and other media for richer effects.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe multimedia collage as a combined-media technique.

questions.prompt: Why should a collage artist consider texture when choosing materials?
options: Texture affects how the surface looks and feels visually
Texture decides the internet password
Texture replaces all colour choices
Texture makes legal issues disappear
questions.correctAnswer: Texture affects how the surface looks and feels visually
questions.explanation: Rough, smooth, shiny or fibrous surfaces change the visual character of a collage.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the effect of texture in collage making.

questions.prompt: Why are ascenders, body height and descenders considered in lowercase calligraphy?
options: They keep letter proportions readable and consistent
They control the firing of clay
They stop fabric from absorbing dye
They replace layout planning
questions.correctAnswer: They keep letter proportions readable and consistent
questions.explanation: Calligraphy depends on consistent letter structure so words remain clear and attractive.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain proportional features of lowercase calligraphy.

questions.prompt: Why is layout important in a poster design?
options: It organises text and images so the message can be read quickly
It changes fabric dye into wax
It fires pottery at a higher temperature
It removes the need for a message
questions.correctAnswer: It organises text and images so the message can be read quickly
questions.explanation: Layout controls placement, spacing and hierarchy so viewers can understand the poster.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of layout in graphic design.

questions.prompt: Why is a two-colour trademark often easier to reproduce than a full-colour illustration?
options: It is simpler, clearer and cheaper to print consistently
It cannot be recognised by viewers
It needs no planning of shape
It must always use photographic detail
questions.correctAnswer: It is simpler, clearer and cheaper to print consistently
questions.explanation: Limited colours help a trademark stay legible across signs, packaging and digital use.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain practical considerations in trademark design.

questions.prompt: Why should a poster have one dominant message?
options: A clear dominant message helps viewers understand the purpose quickly
It makes every detail equally important
It prevents the use of colour
It turns the poster into pottery
questions.correctAnswer: A clear dominant message helps viewers understand the purpose quickly
questions.explanation: Dominance gives priority to the main headline, image or call to action in a poster.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain dominance as a principle in poster design.

questions.prompt: Why does tying fabric before dyeing create a pattern?
options: The tied areas resist some dye, leaving lighter shapes or lines
The knots become permanent beads
The fabric turns into clay
The dye changes into pencil graphite
questions.correctAnswer: The tied areas resist some dye, leaving lighter shapes or lines
questions.explanation: Tight folds and bindings block dye from reaching parts of the cloth.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how resist effects are created in tie and dye.

questions.prompt: Which effect is most associated with twisting fabric from a central point before dyeing?
options: Spiral effect
Pellet effect
Updraught effect
Descender effect
questions.correctAnswer: Spiral effect
questions.explanation: Twisting fabric from a centre and binding it can produce radiating spiral dye patterns.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify tie and dye methods used to create decorative effects.

questions.prompt: Why does wax resist in batik need careful handling?
options: Hot wax and dye processes can cause burns or stains if used carelessly
Wax automatically cleans the workspace
Wax makes sharp tools unnecessary
Wax cannot affect fabric at all
questions.correctAnswer: Hot wax and dye processes can cause burns or stains if used carelessly
questions.explanation: Safe batik work needs controlled heating, protective handling and tidy use of dye materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safety considerations in batik fabric decoration.

questions.prompt: What causes a crackled effect in batik?
options: Cracked wax lets dye enter through fine broken lines
A loom separates warp and weft threads
Clay is kneaded with water
A trademark is scanned into a poster
questions.correctAnswer: Cracked wax lets dye enter through fine broken lines
questions.explanation: When wax cracks, dye seeps through the cracks and leaves fine linear marks.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe characteristics of batik fabric effects.

questions.prompt: Why is clay wedged before modelling a vessel?
options: To remove air pockets and make the clay even
To add calligraphy to the clay
To make the clay permanently wet
To turn clay into fabric
questions.correctAnswer: To remove air pockets and make the clay even
questions.explanation: Wedging improves clay consistency and reduces cracking or bursting during firing.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain clay preparation processes for pottery.

questions.prompt: Why must a clay vase dry slowly before firing?
options: Uneven fast drying can cause cracking or breakage
Slow drying changes it into metal
Drying removes all need for firing
Drying creates a printed poster
questions.correctAnswer: Uneven fast drying can cause cracking or breakage
questions.explanation: Slow, even drying allows moisture to leave without stressing the clay walls.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe drying practice before pottery firing.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes relief sculpture?
options: Forms project from a background surface instead of standing fully free
It is only flat calligraphy on paper
It is fabric dipped in dye
It is a kiln with upward heat flow
questions.correctAnswer: Forms project from a background surface instead of standing fully free
questions.explanation: Relief sculpture is attached to a background while its forms are raised or carved into the surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe relief sculpture as a 3D art form.

questions.prompt: Why should found materials for sculpture be cleaned before use?
options: Cleaning improves hygiene, safety and finish quality
Cleaning makes every material edible
Cleaning removes the need for design
Cleaning turns all materials into clay
questions.correctAnswer: Cleaning improves hygiene, safety and finish quality
questions.explanation: Clean materials are safer to handle and easier to finish neatly in sculpture work.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe preparation of materials for relief sculpture.

questions.prompt: A learner draws a classroom corridor so the floor edges meet at one point on the horizon. Which technique is being applied?
options: One-point perspective
Marbled tie and dye
Plain weaving
Wax removal
questions.correctAnswer: One-point perspective
questions.explanation: A corridor facing the viewer directly commonly uses one-point perspective with one vanishing point.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply one-point perspective to observed spaces.

questions.prompt: A learner sees the corner of a box with two sides going away from the viewer. Which perspective setup is best?
options: Two vanishing points on the horizon line
One woven weft only
A flat wash with no drawing
A single clay pellet
questions.correctAnswer: Two vanishing points on the horizon line
questions.explanation: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points for objects viewed from a corner.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable perspective methods for angular objects.

questions.prompt: A still life includes a bottle, cup and fruit. Which action best begins the drawing process?
options: Observe the arrangement and lightly sketch basic shapes and proportions
Start with heavy dark outlines everywhere
Paste fabric onto the objects
Fire the arrangement in a kiln
questions.correctAnswer: Observe the arrangement and lightly sketch basic shapes and proportions
questions.explanation: Good drawing starts with observation, simple shapes, proportion and placement before detail.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply stages of drawing to a still life composition.

questions.prompt: A learner wants a storage folder for A3 artwork. Which design choice is most suitable?
options: Make a folder slightly larger than A3 with firm covers and secure flaps
Make a folder smaller than A4 to save space
Use wet clay slabs as folder covers
Leave the artwork loose in a school bag
questions.correctAnswer: Make a folder slightly larger than A3 with firm covers and secure flaps
questions.explanation: A portfolio should fit the artwork, protect it from bending and keep pieces together.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply portfolio design requirements for safe artwork storage.

questions.prompt: A learner paints distant hills in a landscape. Which approach best creates atmospheric depth?
options: Use lighter, softer washes for distant areas and stronger tones in the foreground
Use the same dark tone for every area
Cover the whole painting with thick black outlines only
Remove all horizon cues from the painting
questions.correctAnswer: Use lighter, softer washes for distant areas and stronger tones in the foreground
questions.explanation: Distant scenery often appears lighter and less detailed, so wash control can suggest depth.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply wash technique to create depth in scenery painting.

questions.prompt: A learner needs an even blue background for a poster illustration. Which technique is most suitable?
options: Flat wash
Pellet modelling
Relief carving
Plain loom threading
questions.correctAnswer: Flat wash
questions.explanation: A flat wash gives a broad, even colour field suitable for a consistent background.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose a painting technique for an intended visual effect.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to make foliage texture in a painted scenery without painting every leaf. Which method is suitable?
options: Use controlled brush-spray marks in selected areas
Draw only letter descenders
Knead clay repeatedly
Measure warp threads only
questions.correctAnswer: Use controlled brush-spray marks in selected areas
questions.explanation: Brush-spray marks can suggest many small natural textures while keeping the painting efficient.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply brush-spray technique to create texture in painting.

questions.prompt: A painting looks dull because all colours are similar in strength and no area stands out. Which principle should the learner improve?
options: Contrast and dominance
Porosity and vitrification
Warp and weft
Wax cracking only
questions.correctAnswer: Contrast and dominance
questions.explanation: Contrast and dominance help selected areas stand out and give the composition visual focus.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply art principles to improve pictorial composition.

questions.prompt: A collage theme is environmental conservation. Which material choice best supports the theme?
options: Clean reused paper and packaging arranged into a clear image
Freshly cut rare plant leaves from a protected area
Unsorted dirty waste with sharp edges
Only a blank sheet with no pasted material
questions.correctAnswer: Clean reused paper and packaging arranged into a clear image
questions.explanation: Reused clean materials can communicate conservation while keeping the work safe and intentional.
questions.learningOutcome: Select appropriate materials for a PCI-themed collage.

questions.prompt: Which action best creates a painterly effect in a paper collage?
options: Select and arrange torn coloured papers to blend tones like brush marks
Use only straight identical squares with no tone change
Fire the papers in an updraught kiln
Tie the papers with cotton thread before dyeing
questions.correctAnswer: Select and arrange torn coloured papers to blend tones like brush marks
questions.explanation: Torn papers and tonal variation can imitate painted transitions and brush-like texture.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply paper collage methods to create painterly visual effects.

questions.prompt: A learner wants a collage surface to have a slight 3D effect. Which choice is most suitable?
options: Layer thicker materials carefully to raise selected areas
Flatten every material to the same level
Use only a printed title with no image
Wash the support until it tears
questions.correctAnswer: Layer thicker materials carefully to raise selected areas
questions.explanation: Layering selected materials can create relief-like texture while remaining a collage.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply layering to create texture and 3D effects in collage.

questions.prompt: A school seasonal card needs hand lettering that is legible and decorative. Which option best supports the task?
options: Use consistent lowercase calligraphy with clear ascenders, body and descenders
Use random letter heights and crowded spacing
Write the message backwards without purpose
Replace words with pottery pellets
questions.correctAnswer: Use consistent lowercase calligraphy with clear ascenders, body and descenders
questions.explanation: Consistent calligraphy makes the greeting readable while adding visual appeal.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply calligraphy features when illustrating text for a card.

questions.prompt: A learner designs a two-colour trademark for a youth art club. Which feature is most important?
options: Simple memorable symbol and readable lettering
Many tiny details that disappear when reduced
Three unrelated slogans in small type
A complex photograph with no name
questions.correctAnswer: Simple memorable symbol and readable lettering
questions.explanation: A trademark should remain recognisable at different sizes and across media.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply graphic design principles to trademark creation.

questions.prompt: A poster for a school art exhibition must include a scanned trademark. Where should it be placed?
options: Where it supports the layout without overpowering the main message
Across the entire poster so no text can be read
Outside the page margin only
Hidden under a pasted fabric fold
questions.correctAnswer: Where it supports the layout without overpowering the main message
questions.explanation: A trademark should identify the organiser while preserving hierarchy and readability.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply layout planning when integrating a trademark into a poster.

questions.prompt: Which poster choice best uses line and wash illustration?
options: Draw clear outlines and add transparent colour washes to support the message
Use only thick glue with no drawing
Build a clay vase on the poster surface
Tie the poster into a spiral before reading it
questions.correctAnswer: Draw clear outlines and add transparent colour washes to support the message
questions.explanation: Line gives structure, while wash adds colour and tonal interest without hiding the drawing.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply line and wash illustration in poster design.

questions.prompt: A learner wants horizontal stripes on a cotton cloth using tie and dye. Which method is most suitable?
options: Fold or pleat the fabric horizontally and bind it before dyeing
Apply wax only in random dots
Carve the cloth with a chisel
Fire the folded fabric in a kiln
questions.correctAnswer: Fold or pleat the fabric horizontally and bind it before dyeing
questions.explanation: Pleating and tying in a controlled direction can produce linear stripe effects after dyeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply tie and dye methods to create linear effects.

questions.prompt: A learner wants a marbled tie and dye effect. Which approach is most suitable?
options: Crumple the fabric irregularly, bind it and apply dye
Stretch the fabric perfectly flat with no folds
Draw calligraphy body lines on paper only
Join clay pellets in a ring
questions.correctAnswer: Crumple the fabric irregularly, bind it and apply dye
questions.explanation: Irregular crumpling and binding create uneven dye patches associated with marbled effects.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply tie and dye methods to create marbled effects.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best fits a simple tie and dye process?
options: Prepare fabric, tie or bind areas, dye, rinse, dry and finish
Fire clay, carve wood, weave warp, then label a poster
Write a trademark, scan it, then ignore the fabric
Dry fabric first, never add dye, then remove nothing
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare fabric, tie or bind areas, dye, rinse, dry and finish
questions.explanation: Tie and dye needs orderly preparation, resist tying, dyeing and finishing for clean results.
questions.learningOutcome: Sequence practical steps in tie and dye fabric decoration.

questions.prompt: A learner wants a batik fabric with fine crackled lines. Which action helps create that effect?
options: Apply wax, allow it to crack gently, then dye the fabric
Keep wax perfectly unbroken across the whole fabric
Weave thicker weft threads into the fabric
Model the fabric with clay slip
questions.correctAnswer: Apply wax, allow it to crack gently, then dye the fabric
questions.explanation: Dye enters tiny breaks in the wax and forms the crackled batik lines.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply batik processes to create crackled effects.

questions.prompt: A batik design needs some areas to remain the original fabric colour. What should the learner do before dyeing?
options: Cover those areas with wax resist
Scrub those areas with sand
Cut those areas out completely
Write descenders on those areas
questions.correctAnswer: Cover those areas with wax resist
questions.explanation: Wax protects selected areas from dye so the original fabric colour remains after wax removal.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply wax resist to control colour placement in batik.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best prepares clay for pottery after it is collected?
options: Dry, crush, slake, sieve, dry to workable state, then knead and wedge
Paint, scan, print, fold, then write a slogan
Tie, dye, rinse, iron, then carve
Weave, polish, market, then fire the loom
questions.correctAnswer: Dry, crush, slake, sieve, dry to workable state, then knead and wedge
questions.explanation: Clay preparation removes impurities and makes the clay even enough for modelling.
questions.learningOutcome: Sequence clay preparation steps for pottery work.

questions.prompt: A learner models a vase using many small clay balls joined together. Which technique is being used?
options: Pellet technique
Brush-spray technique
Calligraphy technique
Plain weaving technique
questions.correctAnswer: Pellet technique
questions.explanation: The pellet technique builds a form by joining small, similar clay balls into a vessel.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify and apply the pellet technique in hand-built pottery.

questions.prompt: Which action best strengthens joins between clay pellets in a vase?
options: Score, moisten with slip and press pellets firmly together
Dust dry sand between every pellet
Keep pellets different sizes and barely touching
Paint the outside before joining
questions.correctAnswer: Score, moisten with slip and press pellets firmly together
questions.explanation: Scoring and slip help clay surfaces bond so the hand-built vessel is stronger.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply joining methods in pellet-built pottery.

questions.prompt: A class is selecting a safe place for an updraught kiln. Which site is best?
options: An open, well-ventilated area away from flammable materials
Inside a crowded classroom beside curtains
On a wet desk near exercise books
In a narrow passage used as an exit
questions.correctAnswer: An open, well-ventilated area away from flammable materials
questions.explanation: Kiln firing requires ventilation, space and fire safety to protect people and property.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety factors when choosing a kiln location.

questions.prompt: A learner carves a raised animal form on a flat board inspired by Akamba carving. Which artwork type is this?
options: Relief sculpture
Flat wash painting
Tie and dye fabric
Lowercase calligraphy
questions.correctAnswer: Relief sculpture
questions.explanation: The form remains attached to a background surface, so it is a relief sculpture.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the concept of relief sculpture to a practical example.

questions.prompt: A relief sculpture will be made from discarded soft board. Which preparation is best before carving?
options: Clean it, check for hazards and mark the design clearly
Soak it in dye and ignore sharp edges
Heat it in a kiln until it burns
Leave nails and staples in place
questions.correctAnswer: Clean it, check for hazards and mark the design clearly
questions.explanation: Prepared safe material allows controlled carving and improves the final finish.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare recyclable materials for relief sculpture safely.

questions.prompt: A relief sculpture needs a smooth finished surface. Which process is most suitable after carving?
options: Sand and polish or seal the surface appropriately
Leave rough splinters exposed
Cover it with wet clay slip only
Tie it tightly for dyeing
questions.correctAnswer: Sand and polish or seal the surface appropriately
questions.explanation: Finishing removes roughness and can protect the sculpture surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply finishing techniques to relief sculpture.

questions.prompt: In weaving, which threads are held lengthwise on the loom before weaving begins?
options: Warp threads
Weft threads
Descenders
Clay slips
questions.correctAnswer: Warp threads
questions.explanation: Warp threads run lengthwise and provide the structure through which weft threads pass.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic weaving terms and their functions.

questions.prompt: A learner passes a thread over and under alternate warp threads. Which weave is being made?
options: Plain weave
Spiral tie and dye
Pellet build
Flat wash
questions.correctAnswer: Plain weave
questions.explanation: Plain weave is made by alternating weft over and under warp threads.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the over-under sequence used in plain weaving.

questions.prompt: A bracelet design needs beads arranged symmetrically around the centre. Which action best supports the design?
options: Plan the colour and bead sequence before stringing
String beads randomly without checking balance
Use wet clay as thread
Hide the fastening under loose sharp wire
questions.correctAnswer: Plan the colour and bead sequence before stringing
questions.explanation: Planning bead order helps create balance, rhythm and a neat ornamental pattern.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply design planning to jewellery and ornament making.

questions.prompt: A drawing of a box uses one vanishing point, but both side faces are visible equally from a corner view. What is the main problem?
options: A corner view usually needs two-point perspective, not one-point perspective
The box should have no vertical lines
The drawing must be converted to tie and dye
The horizon line should be removed entirely
questions.correctAnswer: A corner view usually needs two-point perspective, not one-point perspective
questions.explanation: When two sides recede from a visible corner, each side normally needs its own vanishing point.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze perspective choices in drawings of angular forms.

questions.prompt: A still life drawing has accurate outlines but looks flat. Which improvement would most directly create form?
options: Add tonal shading based on a clear light source
Add more unrelated objects to the table
Erase every overlap in the composition
Make all object sizes equal
questions.correctAnswer: Add tonal shading based on a clear light source
questions.explanation: Tone from a consistent light source shows volume, shadow and surface direction.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze weaknesses in still life rendering and choose improvements.

questions.prompt: A portfolio folder protects artwork but opens loosely and lets papers fall out. Which feature is missing?
options: Secure flaps, ties or closure to hold work inside
More water on the cover
A wider vanishing point
Extra dye in the folder
questions.correctAnswer: Secure flaps, ties or closure to hold work inside
questions.explanation: A useful portfolio needs a closure system that keeps artworks from slipping or bending.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze functional quality in portfolio folder design.

questions.prompt: A landscape wash has harsh stripes where the learner stopped and restarted unevenly. What is the best correction next time?
options: Work with a wet edge and control water evenly across the wash
Use thicker paper clips as a frame
Apply wax over the whole finished scene
Carve the dry paint with a chisel
questions.correctAnswer: Work with a wet edge and control water evenly across the wash
questions.explanation: Consistent moisture and a wet edge reduce unwanted bands in wash painting.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze technical faults in wash painting and select remedies.

questions.prompt: A brush-spray composition has paint specks covering the main subject and message. Which design decision would improve it?
options: Mask or limit spray areas so texture supports rather than hides the subject
Add more uncontrolled spray over the whole surface
Remove all contrast from the composition
Make the subject the same colour as the background
questions.correctAnswer: Mask or limit spray areas so texture supports rather than hides the subject
questions.explanation: Technique should serve communication; masking and control protect the focal area.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze use of brush-spray technique in pictorial composition.

questions.prompt: A collage about road safety uses many attractive materials but the message is unclear. Which revision is strongest?
options: Create a dominant road-safety symbol and reduce distracting materials
Add more unrelated textures until the surface is full
Remove the theme and keep only decoration
Hide the main image under opaque layers
questions.correctAnswer: Create a dominant road-safety symbol and reduce distracting materials
questions.explanation: A themed collage needs visual hierarchy so materials support the intended message.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze communication effectiveness in PCI-themed collage.

questions.prompt: A multimedia collage uses thick cardboard, beads and fabric, but some pieces are falling off. Which issue is most likely?
options: The adhesive or attachment method does not match the materials
The colours are too harmonious
The theme is too relevant
The work has too much empty space only
questions.correctAnswer: The adhesive or attachment method does not match the materials
questions.explanation: Heavier or textured materials may need stronger adhesive, stitching or mechanical attachment.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze material suitability and attachment methods in collage.

questions.prompt: A seasonal card has beautiful calligraphy but the descenders collide with the line below. What should be adjusted?
options: Line spacing and baseline planning
Kiln ventilation
Clay porosity
Dye temperature only
questions.correctAnswer: Line spacing and baseline planning
questions.explanation: Calligraphy needs planned baselines and spacing so ascenders and descenders remain clear.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze readability problems in calligraphic layout.

questions.prompt: A trademark looks good on a computer screen but becomes unreadable when printed small on a receipt. What is the main design weakness?
options: It depends on details that are too fine for small reproduction
It uses only two colours
It has a clear simple silhouette
It has enough contrast
questions.correctAnswer: It depends on details that are too fine for small reproduction
questions.explanation: Effective trademarks must remain legible and recognisable when reduced.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze scalability and legibility in trademark design.

questions.prompt: A poster headline, image and sponsor mark all compete equally. Which principle is weakest?
options: Dominance
Porosity
Wedging
Plasticity
questions.correctAnswer: Dominance
questions.explanation: Dominance establishes a clear order of importance among poster elements.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze hierarchy in poster design.

questions.prompt: A tie and dye fabric has weak patterns because the dye entered every tied area. What is the likely cause?
options: The fabric was not tied tightly enough to resist dye
The cloth was rinsed after dyeing
The design used cotton fabric
The learner planned a spiral effect
questions.correctAnswer: The fabric was not tied tightly enough to resist dye
questions.explanation: Loose binding allows dye to penetrate areas that were meant to remain lighter.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze causes of weak resist patterns in tie and dye.

questions.prompt: A spiral tie and dye cloth has a centre but no clear radiating movement. What should be improved?
options: Twist fabric evenly from the centre and bind sections before dyeing
Use only one loose knot at the edge
Remove all folds before applying dye
Cut the fabric into separate strips first
questions.correctAnswer: Twist fabric evenly from the centre and bind sections before dyeing
questions.explanation: Controlled twisting and binding create the radial structure needed for a spiral effect.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze method control in spiral tie and dye effects.

questions.prompt: A batik fabric has large unwanted dye patches where clean white areas were expected. Which problem is most likely?
options: Wax resist did not fully cover or seal those areas
The cloth was too carefully labelled
The dye was rinsed after use
The design had too much balance
questions.correctAnswer: Wax resist did not fully cover or seal those areas
questions.explanation: Gaps or thin wax allow dye to enter areas intended to remain protected.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze resist faults in batik fabric decoration.

questions.prompt: A batik piece has a crackled effect everywhere, including areas that needed clean flat colour. Which decision would improve control?
options: Limit intentional cracking to selected waxed areas before dyeing
Crack all wax more deeply across the fabric
Use no wax in any area
Scrape the cloth with carving tools
questions.correctAnswer: Limit intentional cracking to selected waxed areas before dyeing
questions.explanation: Crackled effects are strongest when controlled and placed where they support the design.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze expressive control of crackled batik effects.

questions.prompt: A pellet-built vase cracks along several joins while drying. Which cause is most likely?
options: Pellets were joined poorly or dried unevenly
The learner used a portfolio folder
The vase had a clear focal area
The design had colour harmony
questions.correctAnswer: Pellets were joined poorly or dried unevenly
questions.explanation: Weak joins and uneven drying create stress points that can crack in hand-built pottery.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze faults in pellet-built pottery and their causes.

questions.prompt: A clay sample is very sandy and collapses when shaped. Which property is most inadequate for modelling?
options: Plasticity
Transparency
Calligraphy
Dominance
questions.correctAnswer: Plasticity
questions.explanation: Low plasticity makes clay difficult to shape and retain form during hand-building.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze clay suitability for pottery based on properties.

questions.prompt: An updraught kiln smokes heavily into the working area during firing. Which factor should be checked first?
options: Airflow, chimney path and site ventilation
Letter spacing on the kiln label
The number of poster colours
The shape of calligraphy descenders
questions.correctAnswer: Airflow, chimney path and site ventilation
questions.explanation: An updraught kiln depends on controlled air movement and ventilation for safer firing.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze safety and function issues in updraught kiln firing.

questions.prompt: A relief sculpture has an interesting subject but the raised parts are too shallow to read from a distance. Which issue is involved?
options: Insufficient depth contrast between background and raised forms
Too much fabric dye penetration
Excess calligraphy body height
A perfect plain weave
questions.correctAnswer: Insufficient depth contrast between background and raised forms
questions.explanation: Relief sculpture needs enough projection and shadow to make forms clear.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze form and depth in relief sculpture.

questions.prompt: A learner copies an indigenous relief sculpture exactly and claims it as original work. Which value and practice are weakest?
options: Integrity and respectful acknowledgement of sources
Firing and drying control
Weft tension only
Colour harmony only
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity and respectful acknowledgement of sources
questions.explanation: Artists may learn from cultural works, but they should acknowledge sources and create original responses.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze ethical practice when using indigenous craft as inspiration.

questions.prompt: A woven mat narrows in the middle and edges curve inward. What is the most likely technical cause?
options: Uneven weft tension pulled the warp threads inward
Too much wax was applied in batik
The poster headline was too large
The clay was fired too slowly
questions.correctAnswer: Uneven weft tension pulled the warp threads inward
questions.explanation: Pulling weft too tightly can distort the sides of a woven piece.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze common weaving faults and their causes.

questions.prompt: A learner must create a Visual Arts project on conserving wetlands using drawing and collage. Which plan best integrates both methods?
options: Draw a one-point perspective boardwalk scene, then layer clean reused papers to highlight protected plant and water areas
Make only a plain text slogan with no image
Use random materials without a focal message
Carve a wooden relief and ignore the required 2D methods
questions.correctAnswer: Draw a one-point perspective boardwalk scene, then layer clean reused papers to highlight protected plant and water areas
questions.explanation: The plan combines perspective drawing with themed collage materials to communicate conservation clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an integrated 2D artwork plan using drawing and collage for a PCI theme.

questions.prompt: A Grade 10 group is planning an exhibition display of wash paintings and collages. Which curatorial choice is strongest?
options: Group works by theme, label media clearly and arrange lighting so textures and washes are visible
Stack all artworks on one desk without labels
Place wet paintings behind heavy collages
Display only the largest work and hide the rest
questions.correctAnswer: Group works by theme, label media clearly and arrange lighting so textures and washes are visible
questions.explanation: Good display planning helps viewers compare technique, theme and material quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an effective presentation plan for 2D artworks.

questions.prompt: A learner is designing a poster and trademark for a school art fair. Which design strategy best supports a professional identity?
options: Use a simple two-colour trademark repeatedly, with a clear poster hierarchy and readable calligraphy
Use a different logo, colour and lettering style on every item
Hide the event name in decorative texture
Make all text the same size and weight
questions.correctAnswer: Use a simple two-colour trademark repeatedly, with a clear poster hierarchy and readable calligraphy
questions.explanation: Consistent identity, hierarchy and legibility make graphic communication stronger.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a coordinated graphic identity using trademark, poster layout and calligraphy.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to combine tie and dye with batik on one cotton wall hanging. Which production plan is most sensible?
options: Plan resist areas, test dyes, use controlled tying and wax stages, then rinse and finish safely
Tie and wax randomly without testing colour interaction
Start by firing the cloth in a kiln
Use hot wax with no protective handling or workspace plan
questions.correctAnswer: Plan resist areas, test dyes, use controlled tying and wax stages, then rinse and finish safely
questions.explanation: Combining resist methods requires sequence planning, colour testing and safe handling.
questions.subStrandTitle: Fabric Decoration: Tie and Dye and Batik
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safe plan for combining resist fabric decoration techniques.

questions.prompt: A group wants to make an upcycled relief sculpture inspired by East African carving traditions. Which approach is most respectful and sustainable?
options: Research source traditions, acknowledge inspiration, use safe cleaned waste materials and develop an original subject
Copy a sacred object exactly for sale without context
Collect materials from private land without permission
Use hazardous waste because it looks unusual
questions.correctAnswer: Research source traditions, acknowledge inspiration, use safe cleaned waste materials and develop an original subject
questions.explanation: Respectful craft practice combines research, acknowledgement, originality, safety and environmental care.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an ethical and sustainable plan for relief sculpture inspired by indigenous crafts.

questions.prompt: A learner plans a pellet-built vase for a school display. Which plan best supports strength and appearance?
options: Prepare plastic clay, make uniform pellets, score and slip joins, dry slowly, fire safely and appraise the finish
Use unprepared clay, join dry pellets loosely and fire before drying
Skip design planning and rely only on paint after firing
Build very uneven walls to make drying faster
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare plastic clay, make uniform pellets, score and slip joins, dry slowly, fire safely and appraise the finish
questions.explanation: A strong pottery plan controls clay preparation, construction, drying, firing and review.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a complete production plan for a pellet-built pottery vessel.

questions.prompt: A woven table mat must show rhythm, neat edges and two-colour contrast. Which plan is best?
options: Set even warp tension, alternate weft colours in a planned repeat and maintain consistent edge tension
Change weft tension randomly and ignore the pattern repeat
Use only one loose warp thread for the whole mat
Add dye after weaving to hide all structure
questions.correctAnswer: Set even warp tension, alternate weft colours in a planned repeat and maintain consistent edge tension
questions.explanation: Rhythm and neatness in weaving depend on planned colour repeats and controlled tension.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a weaving plan that applies rhythm, colour contrast and craftsmanship.

questions.prompt: A jewellery project uses beads, recycled metal pieces and leather cord. Which plan best balances beauty, safety and function?
options: Smooth sharp edges, test fastening strength, plan bead rhythm and check comfort when worn
Use sharp scraps directly because they shine
Make the ornament too heavy to wear
Ignore fastenings and rely on weak knots
questions.correctAnswer: Smooth sharp edges, test fastening strength, plan bead rhythm and check comfort when worn
questions.explanation: Good ornament design considers finish, safety, pattern, durability and wearer comfort.
questions.learningOutcome: Create functional and safe jewellery using design principles and appropriate materials.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to market artwork online with integrity. Which strategy is best?
options: Use accurate photos, honest descriptions, clear prices and respect copyright or source acknowledgements
Use misleading filters and claim copied designs as original
Hide material defects from buyers
Use another artist's images without permission
questions.correctAnswer: Use accurate photos, honest descriptions, clear prices and respect copyright or source acknowledgements
questions.explanation: Ethical online marketing depends on truthful information and respect for intellectual property.
questions.learningOutcome: Create ethical strategies for online marketing of artworks.

questions.prompt: A class is preparing a peer critique for pottery, sculpture, weaving and jewellery. Which critique framework is most useful?
options: Discuss materials, technique, design principles, function, safety and suggestions respectfully
Rank friends highest without looking at the work
Comment only on colour and ignore construction
Avoid mentioning improvements to protect feelings
questions.correctAnswer: Discuss materials, technique, design principles, function, safety and suggestions respectfully
questions.explanation: A useful critique combines evidence-based observation, art vocabulary and respectful feedback for improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a fair critique framework for evaluating 3D artworks and crafts.
